name: Rails 7.2 → 8.0 (+ load_defaults 7.2, rspec-rails 8, web-console 4.3)
base_branch: upgrade/phase-13-ruby-3-4 (PR #235; built on 845d5e5, rebased onto 38389c2 — #235's empty 'Retrigger CI after base image 0.9.0 push' commit — before the PR was opened) — stacked; Rails 8.0 needs Ruby >= 3.2, which Phase 13 provides. main is at 10e5c5f (Phases 11 and 12 merged, Rails 7.2.4). Phase 14 (Trixie, Dockerfiles only) and Phase 17 (haml 7, Gemfile + views) were built from the same base in parallel; whichever of this PR and Phase 17 merges second needs a Gemfile.lock rebase

changes.rails: ~> 7.2.0 → ~> 8.0.0; 7.2.4 → 8.0.5.1 (all eleven frameworks; newest 8.0.x on 2026-10-25 per gem_lines.py, released 2026-07-29; 8.0 gets security fixes until 2026-11-07, so Phase 16 (8.1.4) should follow promptly)
changes.rspec_rails: ~> 7.1 → ~> 8.0; 7.1.1 → 8.0.4 (2026-03-11, newest; requires actionpack/activesupport/railties >= 7.2 and allows rspec-* < 5.0). spec/rails_helper.rb already uses config.fixture_paths (Phase 11); no spec change
changes.web_console: unconstrained → ~> 4.3; 4.2.1 → 4.3.0 (Rails-gated: requires railties and actionview >= 8.0.0, held back by Phase 13; drops its activemodel dependency). development.rb's config.web_console.whiny_requests = false is still a 4.3.0 setting (lib/web_console/middleware.rb cattr_accessor)
changes.transitives_moved: none — `bundle lock --update rails rspec-rails web-console --conservative` moved exactly the thirteen gems named above and nothing else
changes.transitives_new: none (uri 1.1.2 was already locked; activesupport 8.0 now declares uri >= 0.13.1)
changes.dependency_edges_changed: actionpack/actionview/railties 8.0 no longer list cgi; actionview no longer lists racc; activesupport adds uri (>= 0.13.1) and drops the < 3 cap on connection_pool and the < 6 cap on minitest; actionpack's rack cap (< 3.3) is gone (rack >= 2.2.4)
changes.transitives_unchanged: rack 3.2.7, rack-session 2.1.2, rackup 2.3.1, rack-test 2.2.0, minitest 5.27.0, zeitwerk 2.8.3, i18n 1.12.0, concurrent-ruby 1.3.8, nokogiri 1.19.4, sprockets 4.4.1 / sprockets-rails 3.5.2, coffee-rails 5.0.0, jquery-rails 4.6.1, active_model_serializers 0.10.16, devise 5.0.4, haml 5.2.2 / haml-rails 2.1.0, puma 8.0.2, pg 1.7.0, omniauth 2.3.1, turbolinks 5.2.1, terser 1.2.8, dartsass-sprockets 3.2.1 / sass-embedded 1.106.1, capybara 3.40.0, shoulda-matchers 8.0.1, simplecov 1.3.2, rubocop 1.92.1 / rubocop-rails 2.38.0
changes.lockfile_platforms: aarch64-linux, ruby, x86_64-linux (unchanged; `bundle lock --add-platform x86_64-linux` then `--add-platform ruby` re-run after the update)
changes.lock_method: Gemfile edited first, then `bundle lock --update rails rspec-rails web-console --conservative` under bundler 2.6.9 in a plain ruby:3.4.12-slim-bookworm container (lock only, no install — this worktree had no dev image yet and building one from the edited Gemfile + old lock would have failed `bundle install`), then the dev image was built from that lock; inside it `bundle check` passes and `bundle list` shows rails 8.0.5.1, rspec-rails 8.0.4, web-console 4.3.0

load_defaults.new_framework_defaults_7_2_rb: deleted (every key was commented out, so each 7.2 default switches on here)
load_defaults.new_framework_defaults_8_0_rb: added verbatim from `rails app:update` (railties 8.0.5.1) with every key commented out — Phase 16 (Rails 8.1) flips load_defaults to 8.0: active_support.to_time_preserves_timezone = :zone, action_dispatch.strict_freshness = true, Regexp.timeout = 1
load_defaults.railties_8_0_5_1_block: `load_defaults "7.2"` in railties 8.0.5.1 is: load_defaults 7.1; self.yjit = true; active_storage.web_image_content_types = png/jpeg/gif/webp; active_record.postgresql_adapter_decode_dates = true; active_record.validate_migration_timestamps = true. It no longer sets active_job.enqueue_after_transaction_commit (listed in the 7.2 defaults file Phase 12 generated from railties 7.2.4): 8.0 deprecates that config key (activejob/lib/active_job/railtie.rb warns if it is set) and ActiveJob::Base.enqueue_after_transaction_commit defaults to false

effects_here.yjit_true: Rails::Application::Finisher's :enable_yjit initializer calls RubyVM::YJIT.enable whenever config.yjit is true and the Ruby supports it — in EVERY environment, not only production (the plan's 'yjit in production' wording is the template comment, not the code). ruby:3.4.12-slim-bookworm is built +YJIT (`ruby --yjit -v` → '+YJIT +PRISM'); a production-mode `rails runner` reports RubyVM::YJIT.enabled? true after boot, and the test suite ran with YJIT on (393 examples green). Expect a modest RSS increase per puma process (YJIT reserves executable memory lazily, --yjit-exec-mem-size defaults to 48 MiB in 3.4); check the pod's memory limit against the first production readings — set `config.yjit = false` in production.rb if the pod is memory-constrained
effects_here.postgresql_adapter_decode_dates_true: PostgreSQLAdapter.decode_dates = true: raw adapter queries (select_value/select_all/exec_query) return Date objects for `date` columns instead of strings. Model attribute reads were always typecast and are unaffected. The only raw query in app/ is the health check's `connection.execute('SELECT 1')` (integer), and the schema has no `date` columns at all (only datetime) — no effect
effects_here.validate_migration_timestamps_true: ActiveRecord::InvalidMigrationTimestampError on a migration whose timestamp is more than a day in the future. All eleven migrations are dated 2018-01-25 … 2018-06-17; the three Active Storage migrations app:update generated (dated today) were rejected — no effect
effects_here.web_image_content_types: Active Storage is not used (no attachments, no tables; its migrations were rejected again) — no effect
effects_here.enqueue_after_transaction_commit: not set by 8.0's 7.2 block (see railties_8_0_5_1_block); app/jobs/application_job.rb is the generator stub and nothing calls perform_later — no effect

not_flipped_here.regexp_timeout: the plan called Regexp.timeout = 1 'a new 8.0 default — keep it'. In railties 8.0.5.1 it is `Regexp.timeout ||= 1` inside `load_defaults "8.0"`, not an unconditional default, so under load_defaults 7.2 it stays nil (confirmed in the production-mode probe). It comes with the 8.0 defaults flip in Phase 16, per the ordering constraint that a defaults flip never ships with the framework bump that introduced it
not_flipped_here.to_time_preserves_timezone: Rails 8.0 warns four times per boot (`to_time` will always preserve the full timezone … in Rails 8.1; called from config/environment.rb:5, i.e. inside initialize!). Setting config.active_support.to_time_preserves_timezone = :zone (the 8.0 default) was tried in a temporary probe and silences all four; left for Phase 16 with the rest of the 8.0 block. Nothing in app/ or spec/ calls to_time
not_flipped_here.strict_freshness: no fresh_when / stale? / etag use in app/ — will be a no-op when Phase 16 flips it

rails_app_update.method: run in a scratch copy inside the dev container (tar the tree to /tmp/scratch, `yes a | bin/rails app:update`, railties 8.0.5.1), diffed against the tree (1621-line diff), applied by hand
